title: Kuei-jin
summary: The vampires of Asia, who live on Chi rather than blood.

claims.text: Kuei-jin is a recent coined word, mostly used by the young, thought to come from Gui Ren, demon people; elders call themselves Wan Kuei, Ten Thousand Demons.
Wan Xian, Ten Thousand Immortals, is said to be the original name. Western Kindred call them Cathayans.
They cannot make ghouls, and those out of balance toward Yang can conceive or father children, called dhampyrs.
Food and drink give no nourishment but can be taken; it takes about ten times a mortal's drink to get one drunk.
Where a generation figure is ever needed, use 13 minus Dharma.

title: Chi
summary: The energy Kuei-jin take in and must keep in balance.

claims.text: The lowest, the chih-mei, take Chi from the flesh of thinking beings; more refined vampires can draw it from breath, spirit or pure essence.
Yin Chi is called black and Yang Chi scarlet.
Too much Yin makes a vampire more corpse-like and inhuman; too much Yang can breed deadly, catching vampiric diseases, such as the Crimson Fever.
A Ch'ing Shih is a vampire overwhelmed by Yin.
A dragon nest is a place of strong Chi where the Wall is 5 or less; a dragon line joins two or more nests, and powerful shen can travel along it.

title: Kuei-jin Weaknesses
summary: How sun, stake and sleep differ for the Kuei-jin.

claims.text: A stake through the heart does not paralyse by itself, but attacks can disrupt the heart's flow of Chi.
Vampires of Yin are vulnerable to wood, and vampires of Yang to metal.
Sunlight rots rather than burns them, and how badly depends on how much Yin they hold.
Torpor is the Little Death: the body dies while the two souls stay inside, beset by visions and open to hostile magic. Many lose their Dharma through it.

title: Hun and P'o
summary: The two souls that replace Conscience, Self-Control and Courage.

claims.text: Kuei-jin have no Conscience, Self-Control or Courage; they use the paired traits Yin and Yang, and Hun and P'o.
Yin is sensitivity to negative energy, Yang receptiveness to positive energy.
Hun is the higher, reasoning soul; P'o is the lower, animal soul, the Demon, close to what Kindred call the Beast.
Shadow Nature is when the P'o rules the body; Wa Nature is the ordinary self. Fire Nature is frenzy and Wave Nature is Rotschreck.

title: Dharma
summary: A Kuei-jin's path to enlightenment.

claims.text: A Dharma is the path to Golconda; elders prefer the older word Di'hana.
An arhat has fully mastered a Dharma. A bodhisattva is one who nearly reaches enlightenment but stays back to help others.
All-Awareness, the Eastern word for Golconda, is the highest state, which very few reach.
A satori is a sudden flash of enlightenment; diao are spells of blindness when a vampire strays from the Way.
Xue was the first and best-known arhat and founded the Fivefold Way.
The Kindred idea of Golconda may be a flawed Cainite reading of Kuei-jin practice.

title: The Second Breath
summary: The Kuei-jin rebirth.

claims.text: The Second Breath is the return from the spirit worlds, the Kuei-jin rebirth.
An urn is a mortal who could become Kuei-jin, or does.
The P'o of one about to become Kuei-jin is taken to Yomi to be tormented.
Many drop their mortal names after the Second Breath for epithets or titles.
Koa is vampiric youth: a mortal lifetime to act as a child before taking up duties under Heaven.

title: Courts, Wu and the Quincunx
summary: How Kuei-jin society is organised.

claims.text: A court is a band of Kuei-jin with shared material or spiritual aims; many hide behind companies, tongs or secret societies. In Japan the word is house, or uji.
A wu is a Kuei-jin family, something like a Sabbat pack.
An ancestor rules a court or region, much like a Western prince; daimyo is the Japanese word.
The Quincunx is an alliance of five major Chinese courts, to which many but not all Chinese courts pay tribute.
The Green Courts hold Korea and nearby China; the Golden Courts cover Southeast Asia and Indonesia, where female Kuei-jin have fared better.
A palace is a meeting place for all Kuei-jin of a region.
A tong is a group of mortals who serve a vampire knowingly; a scarlet screen is a mortal or institution used without knowing.

title: The Five Directions
summary: The duties a Kuei-jin is born to.

claims.text: A direction is a star-born influence on personality and duty; each Kuei-jin has one of five, the four compass points plus the center.
North is the Magistrate, who judges and keeps tradition; south is the Mandator, who carries out the courts' will.
West is the Ghost Dancer, who deals with the spirit worlds; east is the Harvester, who works among mortals.
Center is the Harmonic, who studies the soul and the vampire's own state.

title: The Wheel of Ages
summary: The Kuei-jin view of history as a turning cycle.

claims.text: The world sinks through ever worse ages until the lowest point, then climbs back toward Paradise.
The six ages are Heaven, Beauty, Legends, Beautiful Sadness, Darkness and the coming Age of Sorrow.
The Fourth Age began when the Kuei-jin forsook their duties; human history and their weakness to sun date from it.
The Age of Darkness runs from first contact with the West to now; the Age of Sorrow is close to Gehenna, though most see it as needed.
A Demon Emperor will rise to rule the Sixth Age, replacing the August Personage of Jade; most think it will be one of the Yama Kings.

title: The Yama Kings
summary: Demonic spirit lords older than the Jade Emperor.

claims.text: They hold lands at the far edges of the Yin and Yang Worlds; the West calls those of Yang Banes and those of Yin Malfeans.
In this age they are tied to the P'o and try to bend Kuei-jin to their service; those who fall are akuma, devils.
Yomi is a hell world made from fouled parts of the Yin and Yang Worlds, where the Yama Kings hold domains.

title: The Spirit Courts and the Wall
summary: The Eastern names for the Umbra and its barrier.

claims.text: The Spirit Courts are the unseen realms beside the material world, the source of spirits and Chi; the West calls them the Umbrae.
The Yang World is the higher spirit world of nature spirits and kami; the Yin World is the lower one, home of wraiths and Spectres.
The Ten Thousand Things means all Creation, the Tellurian.

title: The Wall
summary: What divides the world of the living from the realms of spirit.

claims.text: The Wall is the barrier between the Middle Kingdom and the Yin and Yang Worlds, known in the West as the Gauntlet or the Shroud.
In the Middle Kingdom dragon lines lie closer to the surface than in the West; Yang lines are the Moon Bridges, Yin lines the Byways.

title: Words of the Eastern Kindred
summary: Some slang and names of the Kuei-jin.

claims.text: Kin-jin is a scornful word for Western vampires, from a term for people of Caine; Zao-lat is Saulot.
Running Monkeys are Kuei-jin aged 40 or less, and also an insult for Westerners said to act like children forever.
Kyonshi is an insult for a young, brash, Westernised vampire. Shen means any supernatural or Awakened being; hengeyokai are shapeshifters.
Shared terms come mostly from old Chinese, with Japanese, Sanskrit, Korean and other loan words.

title: The Five Dharmas
summary: The five roads of enlightenment.

claims.text: The Howl of the Devil-Tiger is the P'o way, of the South and Fire; the Way of the Resplendent Crane is the Hun way, of the North, Water and Blood.
The Song of the Shadow is the Yin way, of the West, Metal and Bone; the Dance of the Thrashing Dragon is the Yang way, of the East, Wood and Flesh.
The Path of a Thousand Whispers is the way of Balance.

title: Auspicious Occasions and Acts of Blindness
summary: How Dharma rises and falls.

claims.text: At an auspicious occasion the Dharma's Virtue is rolled against P'o: if the Virtue wins the vampire gains a Dharma level; if P'o wins the demon rebels and rules for a scene; if neither, the vampire is discouraged.
After an act of blindness the Virtue is rolled against P'o at a difficulty of permanent Willpower: if the Virtue wins the vampire keeps control; if P'o wins a Dharma level is lost.

title: Benefits of Dharma
summary: What enlightenment brings.

claims.text: Higher Dharma gives a Social dice bonus against Kuei-jin of lower Dharma.
It raises the cap on paired Virtues: at Dharma 6, Hun and P'o, or Yin and Yang, may total 12, split as wished.
It also raises trait maximums, the Chi that may be spent each turn, and rough standing in Kuei-jin society, with few exceptions.

title: Kuei-jin Disciplines
summary: The arts of Chi and soul.

claims.text: Some arts date from the Wan Xian, who used them against the Yama Kings' forces; others arose after the scattering and the karmic curse.
They resemble Kindred powers on the surface but rest on understanding of the vampire's state; learning them takes training, meditation, katas, sutras and talks with spirits.
Kuei-jin learn their powers more slowly than Kindred but gain more versatility, and no bloodline limits what they may learn.

title: Chi Arts
summary: Disciplines that redirect Chi.

claims.text: The four common Chi Arts are Equilibrium (balancing Chi in the body), Tapestry (ambient Chi), Yin Prana and Yang Prana; many scholars count Bone and Flesh Shintai as the Yin and Yang arts.
Using them stirs eddies in the Mirror Lands, and strong uses can disturb the spirit world for days or leave lasting tracks.
A botch on any Chi Discipline draws hostile spirits angered by the disturbance.
Equilibrium can also throw a displeasing person's Chi badly out of balance; most uses need a touch.

title: Kindred Powers Seen from the East
summary: Why the Kuei-jin despise Western Disciplines.

claims.text: Most Kuei-jin think Kindred Disciplines deeply unnatural: Kindred call on their Blood carelessly and bend Chi wherever they use it.
The ripples upset spirits and sensitive Kuei-jin, and many believe they hasten the decay of the Great Cycle, another reason to drive the foreigners out.

title: Projected Powers
summary: Hitting a target with sprays and flames.

claims.text: To strike with a cloud, spray or gout, roll Stamina + Athletics or Firearms; range is 10 feet per Strength dot, and Demon Chi can extend it.
The target may dodge as usual, and if hit resists as the power says.

title: Black Wind
summary: A Demon Art of speed and savagery.

claims.text: Like every Demon Art it is violent: it must serve deeds that fit the P'o, such as attacking or moving at great speed, never playing a guitar quickly.

title: Blood Shintai
summary: Mastery of the body's flowing blood.

claims.text: Followers may be attuned to Yin, Yang or Balance, seeing Yin and Yang as ever-moving flows rather than fixed amounts, like blood through the body.

title: Jade Shintai
summary: Becoming a conduit for elemental Chi.

claims.text: Instead of focusing personal energy, the vampire channels the ambient Chi of the elements and takes on qualities of jade, held in legend to be a soul substance.

title: The Wan Xian
summary: The Ten Thousand Immortals before the fall.

claims.text: The Wan Xian were chosen for wisdom, power and balance, part mortal and part spirit; a soul crossed into the spirit worlds and came back to become one.
They fed on Chi drawn moderately from the world, drove the Yama Kings' servants away, and watched over the first human settlements of Tibet and the Yellow River valley.

In the Third Age some learned Chi could be taken from other beings; they began with demons and enemies, but hunger grew, warlords and death cults rose, and they even set the hengeyokai against one another.
The spirit worlds drew back from the Middle Kingdom in fear of their greed.

title: The Great Principle
summary: The code of the Grand Arhat.

claims.text: Xue, called the Grand Arhat, found Golconda once the Wan Xian had fallen; the code Xue followed, drawn from revelation and meditation, became the Great Principle.

title: Fallen Courts
summary: Courts lost to corruption and folly.

claims.text: The Tortoise Court was corrupted by akuma, because two Yama Kings, Ton Mu and Mikaboshi, had made a wager, and ceased to be.
The White Tiger Court broke apart when its empress went into forbidden Tibet seeking holy places.
